title: Choose the three-month article's visual world
question: How should 500 focused hours compressed into 90 days feel? Lock a world, steer it, or re-roll.

options.label: The Fluency Protocol
options.thesis: The three-month claim becomes a transparent experiment whose inputs, assumptions, and result the reader can pressure-test.
options.viewport: A full-height protocol sheet opens with 500 HOURS ÷ 90 DAYS = 5H 34M/DAY, Aljohn's portrait clipped beside the formula, and a live compression slider embedded in the page rather than inside a dashboard card.
options.risk: Can feel clinical if Aljohn's first-person voice and humor do not keep breaking through the measurements.

raised.raise: Every claim now resolves into a numbered, visible step rather than a decorative section.
One fixed 90-day progress rail controls the whole reading journey.
The calculator result receives one deliberately calm, high-contrast field amid denser evidence.

options.label: The 90-Day Training Camp
options.lineage: boxing-gym round clocks, coach clipboards, and training logs
options.thesis: Learning in three months is framed as an intense but adjustable training camp, not a miracle shortcut.
options.viewport: A giant 90-day clock and 500-hour training prescription dominate the first screen; the reader sets daily training time immediately and sees the finish date move.
options.risk: The most familiar direction, and its intensity can accidentally turn honest expectations into hustle culture.

options.label: Build Fluency, Step by Step
options.thesis: Hours, practice, immersion, and feedback become pieces assembled in strict order.
options.viewport: The opening formula is an exploded four-piece build; scrolling clicks each new piece into the 90-day plan while the calculator previews the completed model.
options.case: Product clarity is excellent; adult readers may identify less strongly with a toy-instruction world than with a real study protocol.
options.risk: Can trivialize the sacrifice and uncertainty in Aljohn's actual experience.

options.label: The No-Bullshit Study Zine
options.thesis: A friend with a marker dismantles the three-month claim in plain language, one annotated spread at a time.
options.viewport: The formula is scrawled across a two-page spread with Aljohn's notes, a stopwatch diagram, and the first calculator control highlighted like the line that matters.
options.case: Audience identification is high and the voice feels human; its informal drawing language gives up some authority on research-heavy passages.
options.risk: Can become cute or visually noisy when the article needs sober numerical clarity.

options.label: The Cutting Bench
options.thesis: Ninety days scrub past as frames, with deliberate hours selected and wasted time hanging below as trims.
options.viewport: A horizontal 90-frame rail crosses the hero and the stopping point is marked by tape.
options.case: The progress rail is powerful, but editing vocabulary obscures the language-learning mechanism.
options.risk: The metaphor requires explanation before it helps.
options.kept: One persistent progress rail now paces the assigned protocol.

options.label: The Deployed Schedule
options.thesis: Changing one daily-hours input expands or compresses the entire learning schedule.
options.viewport: A compact 90-day packet unfolds into the full plan as the reader drags one control.
options.case: The responsive mechanism is elegant, but the abstract paper geometry weakens immediate comprehension.
options.kept: The calculator propagates one input across every result in real time.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished long-form learning article with a portrait hero, research callouts, clean charts, and a calculator card.
canonCard.viewport: Headline, concise deck, Aljohn portrait, and one blue calculator button above a conventional article column.
canonCard.risk: Clear and familiar, but interchangeable with thousands of language-learning blogs.
